title: Portable edge-proxy template for restricted on-prem customers
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers with strict egress restrictions, intermittent bastion access, or fully air-gapped networks frequently request bespoke connectivity solutions to bootstrap Redwood Private installations. These requests stall onboarding, create costly one-off engineering work, and increase time-to-revenue.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight, auditable "edge-proxy" template and onboarding recipe that product teams can offer as a self-serve connector for common restricted-network patterns. The deliverable should: (1) reduce bespoke engineering by providing a hardened template; (2) include a preflight checker to flag incompatible network constraints; (3) provide explicit upgrade and rollback guidance for customers who cannot allow continuous outbound connections; and (4) preserve auditability for enterprise compliance teams.
background: We see repeated customer requests where network teams will only permit periodic outbound connections, strictly limit ports, or mandate proxy-only egress via corporate appliances. Current intake paths route these to Solutions Eng + Eng on an ad-hoc basis which causes long waits and duplicate work. Existing assets (network-runbooks, proxy samples) exist but are scattered and assume either full internet egress or a private bastion with SSH access. This template is intended to bridge the gap for the most common constrained patterns without building bespoke adapters per customer.
proposed_solution: Ship a tested and documented 'Portable Edge-Proxy' reference bundle composed of: 1) a small single-binary connector (Go-based) that runs inside customer network as an outbound-only component and supports manifest-signed operations; 2) a preflight network probe (script + container) customers can run to produce a compatibility report; 3) an upgrade bundle workflow that packages updates as signed tarballs delivered via customer-approved storage (S3 presigned, internal HTTP mirror, or USB/airgap manifest); 4) a short-run playbook for Solutions/Onboarding that maps preflight results to recommended engagement lanes. The connector will support three operation modes: periodic-poll (for high-restriction environments), proxy-proxied (for corp proxies with auth), and bastion-relay (when temporary inbound access is permitted).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A runnable connector binary and Docker image with basic TLS auth, metrics endpoint, and audit events documented.
2) Preflight script produces structured compatibility report and a human-readable remediation checklist.
3) Onboarding runbook and customer-facing docs published in the Confluence 'Private Deploy' space.
4) Pilot completed with 2 enterprise customers (one proxy-limited, one periodic-poll) and feedback captured.
5) Engineering owner accepts the connector repo and adds a CI job that produces signed release artifacts.
6) Security review completed and S3/offline manifest upgrade flow validated.
out_of_scope: Full VPN or managed IPsec tunnels, permanent Redwood-hosted bastions inside customer network, and bespoke protocol brokers for unusual middleboxes. This work does not attempt to solve every bespoke corporate firewall rule set — rather, it addresses the top 3 recurring patterns observed during intake.
risks:
- Connector could be misconfigured, creating telemetry blindspots.
- Customers might expect 24/7 live support for airgapped upgrades.
- Security review may require cryptographic changes to manifest signing, delaying delivery.
- Legal/regulatory constraints could prohibit storing upgrade artifacts even temporarily in third-party object stores for some customers.
stakeholders: Product: Marco Liao (assignee), Solutions Eng: Priya Desai, Security: Lena Ortiz, Legal: Tom Baker, Infra Eng: Keenan Park, UX: Riley Chen
tasks:
1) Engineering spike: prototype connector modes (3 days).
2) Build preflight script and sample reports (2 days).
3) Write onboarding runbook and customer-facing guide (3 days).
4) Security review and threat model update (5 days).
5) CI for signed release artifacts and Docker image (3 days).
6) Pilot onboarding with two customers; collect feedback and close loop (2 sprints).
7) Docs polish and publish (1 sprint).
success_metrics:
- Time from intake to first successful private deploy reduced by 30% for constrained-network customers.
- Number of bespoke network-engagements handled by Solutions Eng reduced by 40% within quarter.
- Pilot customers rate the connector onboarding >= 4/5 for clarity and security.
- Connector CI produces signed artifacts with reproducible builds.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Prototype + internal testing (2 sprints).
Phase 2: Security review and pilot with two customers (1 quarter).
Phase 3: General availability as a 'self-serve template' with checkboxes in the intake form and a preflight link in the onboarding portal.
Phase 4: Iterate on additional middlebox adapters if pilot metrics justify further investment.
